limits.value: 100 MB disk quota on the free account
128 MB memory limit per free account

identity_cost.detail: five steps, and step five is 'IRL Verification. Enter your personal cell/mobile phone number to receive an SMS with a verification code.' Before that: email verification, a 20-question quiz, an IRC NickServ registration, and two existing users must vouch for you, which cannot happen within one hour of creating the signup account. No card.

evidence.proved: TCP connect to port 2222 timed out at 16.4 s and again at 30 s from this host, so reachability is not established from here
the Free column caps memory at 128 MB, processes at 100, SSH sessions at 6 and background processes at 2
quoted: '5. IRL Verification. Enter your personal cell/mobile phone number to receive an SMS with a verification code.'
quoted: '4. Get two registered users to vouch (approve) you.' and 'It will take atleast 1 hour before your free account can be activated.'
quoted: 'Disk Quota 100 MB', 'Memory limit 128 MB', and 'Listen TCP/UDP port (custom server)' checked only in the Supporter column

record.notes: The cleanest rejection in evaluated offerings: a mobile number and two human vouches, for 100 MB. A supporter account at EUR 3 a month skips the queue but still requires the SMS step, per the same page.

session_cap.note: no session cap published; detach with screen or tmux is allowed

extras.shape_note: 100 MB and a 128 MB memory limit, both in the vendor's MB
extras.price_arithmetic: no charge for the free account; supporter is from EUR 3 a month

record.confidence_note: all five steps and the account table are quoted from Blinkenshell's own pages read.
record.binding_note: the port allowance is the feature that would make it a machine, and it is behind the paid tier; the disk quota is secondary.

probe.note: the saved run this record cites: a timeout on both ports
